result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B is sharper about what the call must achieve: its gate check requires a problem she can size, a named signer and her commitments. It also handles decision authority well by having the seller confirm it early and ask who else weighs in. A has the better cost-of-failure framework, worked out with her using her own numbers, plus ramen-specific details, but it treats decision-makers more lightly and a few of its questions can be answered yes or no. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A states what has to be true by the end of the call, including a gate check. It also verifies early who signs and ends with a dated next step and a set time for the follow-up summary. B is broader and gives a better cost framework that it works out with her, using her numbers. However, its goal and its question about who else decides are looser, and it never says when to raise who approves the purchase. Both answers include some yes/no questions, and neither invents facts.
